model: claude-sonnet-5-5 in a Claude Code session
system: You are a careful experimenter who designs measurements. You can only use the tools you are given, and only a limited number of measurements. Choose each measurement so that it helps to tell the two models apart, and say why. At the end say which model the measurements favour and how sure you are, or say that they do not tell the models apart. Do not say that a model is true because it fits.
task: A block of 2 kg slides on a table and slows down; the launcher of this rig cannot start it faster than 2 m/s. Two models of the drag compete: linear drag, v = v0 exp(-g t), and quadratic drag, v = v0 / (1 + k v0 t), with g and k unknown. Each reading of the speed has a standard uncertainty of 0.1 m/s. Choose at most 8 measurements, with a start speed of at most 2 m/s, that tell the two models apart.

steps.text: With a launcher limited to 2 m/s the quadratic effect is small: at 2 m/s and 10 s the loss from k v0 t is about one. The models are furthest apart at long times and at the highest speed the rig allows, so I measure there and add a repeat to see the noise: 2 m/s at 10 s twice (repeat 1 and 2), 2 m/s at 5 s, and 1 m/s at 10 s.

The readings are 1.15, 0.97, 1.44 and 0.80 m/s. The two readings at 2 m/s and 10 s differ by 0.18 m/s, which is the noise. I spend the other four on the same idea: 0.5 m/s at 10 s, 1.5 m/s at 10 s, 1 m/s at 5 s, and 2 m/s at 2 s as a short one.

The build's fits favour quadratic drag: chi-square about 14 for 7 degrees of freedom against about 28 for linear drag, a difference of about 14, with k near 0.041 per metre and a standard error of about 0.004. A difference of 14 is below the 25 that this lesson counts as telling the models apart, so the measurements do not tell them apart. I would not report a model. The limit is the rig: with starts of at most 2 m/s, eight readings at this noise cannot separate the models, and a launcher that reaches 10 m/s or more would.
